UnitStatement: DEL-17-07 has Deliverable ID DEL-17-07 within Package ID PKG-17 (Export Format Interoperability).
DEL-17-07 is of type BACKEND_FEATURE_SLICE.
DEL-17-07 covers scope items SOW-030 and SOW-074.
DEL-17-07 addresses objectives OBJ-009, OBJ-017, and OBJ-018.
DEL-17-07 defines the first conservative PCF export slice for broader plant-design interoperability.
DEL-17-07 is not the first validation backbone, not a complete PCF implementation, not a CAEPIPE compatibility claim, and not professional validation evidence.
The target family is PCF subset export, bounded by PLAN-EXPORT-INTEROP section 5. PCF and CAEPIPE public PCF translator documentation.
The primary output is a PCF target file plus export package records required by DEL-17-02: manifest, stable ID map, diagnostics, and loss report.

Initial subset candidates are straight pipe, elbows/bends, tees, reducers, flanges, valves, end connections, line numbers, nominal size, OD/wall-thickness attributes where supported, basic spec/material labels, coordinates, component identifiers, and stable ID sidecar mapping.
Unsupported, approximated, delegated, omitted, and TBD behavior shall be visible in the loss report.
Hidden translator defaults shall not be silently relied on; they shall be rejected, warned, delegated, or recorded as TBD/loss-report entries.

The version/profile basis is TBD; no first supported PCF target profile or CAEPIPE translator version is selected in this phase, and closure requires admitted public evidence or explicit human project authority.

The future PCF subset profile shall include a classification record before writer implementation, defining the required record shape without finalizing support status while the target version/profile basis remains TBD.
Straight pipe is classified TBD on evidence from PLAN-EXPORT-INTEROP section 5. PCF, the CAEPIPE-PCF component mapping table, and DEL-17-01 TBD-17-01-005, and is required before export acceptance.
Elbows and bends are classified TBD on PLAN-EXPORT-INTEROP section 5. PCF and the CAEPIPE-PCF component mapping table, required before export acceptance.
Tees and branches are classified TBD; branch/SIF semantics remain bounded by project data-boundary controls, required before export acceptance.
Reducers are classified TBD on PLAN-EXPORT-INTEROP section 5. PCF and the CAEPIPE-PCF component mapping table, required before export acceptance.
Flanges are classified TBD on PLAN-EXPORT-INTEROP section 5. PCF and the CAEPIPE-PCF translator flange handling option, required before export acceptance.
Valves are classified TBD on the CAEPIPE-PCF translator valve handling option and component mapping table, required before export acceptance.

End connections, free ends, equipment nozzles, and adjacent pipelines are TBD/delegated/unsupported until profile decision; solver-ready boundary semantics must be blocked or loss-reported when not preserved.
Line numbers, nominal size, coordinates, and component identifiers are classified TBD and required for traceability when exported.
OD and wall thickness attributes are TBD/delegated when external mapping is needed; missing or externally mapped values require diagnostics/loss entries.
Basic spec/material labels are TBD/delegated for target property mapping; material property mapping must not be silently inferred.
Supports and restraints are TBD/delegated/unsupported unless the profile proves preservation, and are listed separately in the export report and loss report.
Stable ID sidecar mapping is a candidate exported sidecar, required where direct PCF carriage is not source-confirmed.

PCF-to-CAEPIPE conversion can depend on translator dialog fields such as piping code, specific gravity, node numbering, size filtering, vertical axis, flange handling, and valve handling; DEL-17-07 shall not encode those as hidden OpenPipeStress defaults.
Unit interpretation depends on PCF UNITS-BORE; the profile shall declare PCF unit policy and produce diagnostics when source units cannot be represented explicitly.

Temperature, pressure, fluid density, weights, OD, wall thickness, support type, and material mapping have translator-specific fallback behavior; missing values and fallback sources shall be reported rather than silently supplied by the exporter.

Free ends may be anchored by CAEPIPE translator behavior because PCF lacks certain connection details; end-connection and boundary-condition semantics shall be marked explicit, unsupported, delegated, or TBD with no solver-ready restraint claim from PCF alone.

Some PCF component identifiers are simulated in CAEPIPE as rigid elements, equivalent pipes, concentrated masses, or other approximations; component coverage shall distinguish direct export from downstream approximation and record affected canonical IDs.

The PCF subset profile shall declare profile ID, target family, target version basis, units, coordinates, supported entity families, delegated behavior, unsupported behavior, and TBD behavior, and shall consume DEL-17-01 and DEL-17-02.
The PCF writer shall emit only the conservative subset selected by the profile; unsupported or unresolved entities shall not be silently omitted.

The unsupported behavior report shall include loss-report categories required by DEL-17-02 with affected canonical IDs, target artifact reference if any, reason, source-basis reference, and downstream implication.

Invented fixtures shall be original/invented only and shall not reproduce proprietary models, protected standards data, vendor examples, owner criteria, protected pipe tables, material allowables, SIF/flexibility tables, or commercial catalog values.
DEL-17-01 is the source authority providing admitted source IDs, PCF caveats, and unresolved questions for DEL-17-07.
DEL-17-02 provides the common export package, profile, stable ID map, manifest, and loss-report contract.
DEL-03-02 is a declared upstream dependency for component/section source data contracts; implementation use remains TBD until consumed.
DEL-13-04 is a declared upstream dependency for transformation/loss semantics; implementation use remains TBD until consumed.
DEL-15-02 is a declared upstream dependency for handoff-package alignment; implementation use remains TBD until consumed.
PLAN-EXPORT-INTEROP (plans/EXPORT_FORMAT_INTEROPERABILITY_PLAN.md) is the source for PCF target priority, conservative subset candidates, and risk framing.
CAEPIPE-PCF (https://www.sstusa.com/pdfs/PCF.pdf) is public evidence for PCF translator behavior, defaults, mappings, and caveats.
The exporter should help users exchange plant-design geometry and component context while making every unsupported, approximate, delegated, or unknown behavior visible.

PCF is a secondary interoperability path in the PKG-17 strategy and should not be treated as the first deterministic solver-validation backbone, given documented translator fallback and mapping behavior.

Start from the plan-listed conservative subset: straight pipe, elbows/bends, tees, reducers, flanges, valves, end connections, line numbers, nominal size, OD/wall-thickness where supported, basic spec/material labels, coordinates, component identifiers, and stable ID sidecar mapping.
Do not expand the subset because a downstream translator might infer something; if source evidence does not confirm the behavior, mark it TBD, unsupported, or delegated.

CAEPIPE PCF translator default or external behaviors (units, load data, specific gravity, weight, OD/wall thickness, support/material mapping, boundary conditions, component simulation) are target-path facts, not OpenPipeStress exporter defaults.
For this deliverable a hidden default is a reportable condition.
If OpenPipeStress has explicit source data and the PCF profile can carry it, export it.
If the target path may infer behavior from translator configuration, record delegated behavior.
If a behavior affects solver-ready interpretation and is not source-confirmed, block or mark TBD.
If a component is represented by a target-side approximation, record the approximation and affected canonical IDs.

Stable ID sidecars are expected for this slice unless direct PCF identity carriage is later source-confirmed, connecting canonical model IDs to target records, omitted entries, diagnostics, and loss-report rows.

Support/restraint semantics should be reviewed separately from geometry/component export, and the first exporter should not imply reliable support preservation unless the profile explicitly proves it.
Public PCF translator evidence indicates support transfer can depend on PCF attributes, SKEY values, mapping databases, options, stiffness/gap/friction customization, or default hanger behavior.

Support/restraint is Reliably preserved when the profile has source-confirmed PCF attributes, mapping rules, units, coordinates, support type, stiffness/gap/friction semantics, and stable ID traceability for the class.
Support/restraint is Delegated when the downstream translator or user-owned mapping database may decide final support type or properties without local support preservation.
Support/restraint is TBD when public/project-owned evidence does not yet resolve whether the profile can preserve the class.
Support/restraint is Unsupported when the profile cannot carry the required semantics or the project intentionally excludes the class.
Support/restraint is Blocked when loss of support/restraint meaning would make the package misleading for solver-ready or compatibility-sensitive use.
Support/restraint classification belongs in the profile and loss report, not in hidden writer defaults.
Successful PCF file creation is export evidence only, not proof of correct downstream import, complete stress-model semantics, code compliance, or professional acceptance.
Require explicit unit policy; do not use dimensionless or missing unit metadata as fallback.
Prefer explicit source OD and wall thickness attributes where supported; external mapping database fallback is delegated target behavior, not local data.
Do not create pressure and temperature load values from translator defaults; missing values remain diagnostics, TBD, or loss-report entries.
Material/spec labels may be exported if source-owned, but target material property mapping remains delegated unless source-confirmed.
Direct component export and target-side simulation are different conditions; record approximations.
Avoid implying boundary-condition preservation for free ends and equipment connections when PCF lacks connection detail.
CAEPIPE-PCF behavior may be documented as a secondary route only and must not become a compatibility claim.
A narrow profile with strong diagnostics avoids hidden behavior and supports auditability, at the cost of some models exporting with many unsupported/TBD entries.
A sidecar stable ID map preserves traceability when PCF cannot carry canonical IDs directly, but requires consumers to keep target file and sidecar together.
Blocking support/restraint ambiguity reduces risk of misleading stress-model handoff but limits usefulness for tools that tolerate inferred support behavior.
Invented-only fixtures preserve IP and standards boundaries but do not prove compatibility with real proprietary plant models.
No proprietary, vendor, standards-derived, or client examples are admitted; future examples should use small invented models with artificial names, dimensions, units, and provenance.

This procedure describes how to produce and use the conservative PCF subset exporter deliverable without relying on hidden translator defaults or making unsupported interoperability claims.
Prerequisite: DEL-17-01 source basis has been consumed for PCF source evidence and unresolved questions.
Prerequisite: DEL-17-02 export package/profile/stable-ID/loss-report contract has been consumed.
Prerequisite: declared upstream dependencies DEL-17-02, DEL-03-02, DEL-13-04, and DEL-15-02 are reviewed.
Prerequisite: PCF source behavior is limited to accessible public/project-owned evidence.
Prerequisite: fixture data is invented or otherwise redistribution-safe.
Prerequisite: no protected standards text, proprietary examples, private project data, commercial solver files, or license-bypass instructions are used.
Step 1: read DEL-17-01 Source_Basis_Register.md and CAEPIPE_Question_Dossier.md.
Step 1: read DEL-17-02 Specification.md for profile, ID-map, manifest, and loss-report requirements.
Step 1: read plans/EXPORT_FORMAT_INTEROPERABILITY_PLAN.md section 5. PCF.
Step 1: read the admitted public PCF translator source slices before making any PCF behavior claim.
Step 1: mark unsupported, source-absent, or version-sensitive behavior as TBD.
Step 2: create a profile record for the PCF target family.
Step 2: declare profile ID, profile version, target version basis, source-basis IDs, and boundary notes.
Step 2: declare unit policy, coordinate policy, identity policy, supported entity families, and loss-report policy.
Step 2: classify each candidate entity family as exported, omitted, approximated, delegated, unsupported, or TBD.
Step 2: keep target version/profile basis as TBD until public evidence or human project authority resolves it.
Step 3: start from the plan-listed subset only.

Step 3: keep straight-pipe, bend, tee, reducer, flange, valve, end-connection, line/component identity, nominal-size, OD/wall-thickness, material/spec label, coordinate, and stable-ID behavior separate in the profile.
Step 3: require explicit unit-bearing and provenance-bearing source data for exported physical values.
Step 3: move support/restraint semantics to separate handling unless the selected profile proves reliable preservation.
Step 3: do not add hidden defaults for missing pressure, temperature, fluid density, component weight, material properties, support type, or boundary conditions.
Step 4: emit only profile-supported PCF records.
Step 4: emit deterministic ordering where the profile and package contract require it.
Step 4: preserve canonical IDs directly only when source-confirmed; otherwise write a stable ID sidecar.
Step 4: produce diagnostics when required source data is missing, ambiguous, unsupported, or delegated.
Step 4: produce a loss report for every export attempt.
Step 4: keep PCF writing inside the approved deliverable write scope for the implementation tranche.
Step 5: use invented model names, line IDs, component IDs, coordinates, and unit-bearing values.
Step 5: record fixture provenance and redistribution status.
Step 5: include positive cases for supported subset records.
Step 5: include negative cases for unsupported supports/restraints, ambiguous units, missing OD/wall thickness, unsupported components, and unresolved boundary conditions.
Step 5: do not use proprietary plant models, vendor examples, protected standards data, owner criteria, commercial catalog values, material allowables, or SIF/flexibility data.

Fixture provenance records should use a minimum template before any fixture is admitted, covering Fixture ID, purpose, invented model name, invented line/component IDs, coordinates and unit-bearing values, entity classes covered, redistribution status, contributor certification, and review disposition.
Fixture redistribution status uses values public_permissive, private_only, unknown, or protected_suspected as applicable.
Step 6: confirm the PCF target file is emitted only for supported profile content.
Step 6: confirm the manifest references the profile, source basis, target file, stable ID sidecar, diagnostics, and loss report.
Step 6: confirm the stable ID sidecar links canonical IDs to emitted target records or loss-report entries.
Step 6: confirm every unsupported, approximated, delegated, omitted, or TBD behavior appears in the loss report.
Step 6: confirm no release, compatibility, code-compliance, formal-validation, or professional-acceptance claim is present.

Step 6: confirm generated PCF export evidence is not described as downstream import compatibility, solver validation, release readiness, code compliance, professional acceptance, or external-tool approval.
Phase A verification confirms the four-document kit exists.
Phase A verification checks the default section headings required by the four-documents skill.
Phase A verification checks that source-grounding gaps remain TBD, assumptions, or conflict-table entries.
Phase A verification checks that no implementation code, schema files, protected standards data, proprietary examples, or professional/release/compatibility claims were introduced.
Future implementation verification remains TBD and should be defined only after the PCF profile and writer tranche are sealed.

The deliverable should retain or produce a PCF subset profile, PCF target file, export manifest, stable ID sidecar map, diagnostics, loss report, invented fixture provenance records, and run records for TASK execution and validation.
DEL-17-07 shall define and later implement a conservative PCF subset exporter producing a PCF subset profile, PCF writer behavior, unsupported behavior report, and invented fixtures.

DEL-17-07 shall not claim PCF completeness, CAEPIPE compatibility, solver validation, release readiness, code compliance, professional acceptance, or formal external-tool approval, and shall not implement schema changes or code in this Phase A four-document pass.
DEL-17-07-REQ-001: the PCF subset profile shall consume DEL-17-01 as the source-basis authority for PCF target behavior claims.
DEL-17-07-REQ-002: the PCF subset profile shall consume DEL-17-02 for export package, profile, stable ID map, manifest, and loss-report rules.
DEL-17-07-REQ-003: target behavior not supported by admitted public/project-owned evidence shall remain TBD, delegated, unsupported, or loss-reported.
DEL-17-07-REQ-004: the exporter shall not rely on hidden translator defaults for stress-relevant or identity-relevant behavior.
DEL-17-07-REQ-010: the PCF profile shall declare target_family = PCF and include profile ID, profile version, target version basis, source-basis IDs, and boundary notes.
DEL-17-07-REQ-011: the PCF profile shall declare unit policy, coordinate policy, stable-ID policy, line/component identity policy, and loss-report policy.
DEL-17-07-REQ-012: the target version basis shall remain TBD until public evidence or human project authority selects a first PCF target profile.
DEL-17-07-REQ-013: the profile shall classify each candidate entity family as exported, omitted, approximated, delegated, unsupported, or TBD.
DEL-17-07-REQ-014: the initial candidate subset shall be limited to the plan-listed PCF entities and attributes unless later source review narrows or expands it.
DEL-17-07-REQ-015: the PCF profile shall carry DEL-17-01, DEL-17-02, CAEPIPE-PCF, and PLAN-EXPORT-INTEROP source-basis references; missing references shall block package acceptance.
DEL-17-07-REQ-020: the PCF writer shall emit only profile-supported content from unit-aware, provenance-bearing OpenPipeStress model data.

DEL-17-07-REQ-021: the writer shall produce diagnostics for missing or ambiguous units, coordinates, nominal size, OD, wall thickness, material/spec labels, component identity, end-connection data, and support/restraint semantics when those fields affect the selected profile.

DEL-17-07-REQ-022: the writer shall not invent pressure, temperature, fluid density, component weight, OD, wall thickness, material properties, support type, equipment connection, or boundary-condition data.

DEL-17-07-REQ-023: the writer shall preserve canonical OpenPipeStress identity through target metadata when explicitly supported or through a sidecar stable ID map when direct PCF carriage is not source-confirmed.
DEL-17-07-REQ-024: the writer shall record target-generated identity separately from canonical OpenPipeStress identity.
DEL-17-07-REQ-030: every PCF export attempt shall produce or reference a loss report.

DEL-17-07-REQ-031: loss report entries shall include affected canonical IDs, category, severity, target artifact if any, reason, source-basis reference, and downstream implication, consistent with DEL-17-02.
DEL-17-07-REQ-032: support/restraint semantics shall be listed separately when the PCF target path cannot preserve them reliably.

DEL-17-07-REQ-033: free-end, equipment-nozzle, adjacent-pipeline, and boundary-condition semantics shall be blocked, TBD, delegated, or loss-reported when the target path would otherwise depend on translator anchoring or incomplete PCF connection data.

DEL-17-07-REQ-034: component mappings known to become target-side rigid elements, equivalent pipes, concentrated masses, or other approximations shall be recorded as approximated or delegated behavior rather than direct support.
DEL-17-07-REQ-040: fixtures shall be invented or otherwise redistribution-safe with documented provenance.

DEL-17-07-REQ-041: fixtures shall not copy proprietary plant models, vendor examples, protected standards text, protected tables, material allowables, SIF/flexibility values, owner criteria, or commercial catalog values.
DEL-17-07-REQ-042: public fixtures shall avoid code-specific compliance semantics and shall not imply professional acceptance.

Public CAEPIPE PCF translator documentation (CAEPIPE-PCF) is an accessible source for translator behavior, defaults, and mappings, but not authority for OpenPipeStress completeness or compatibility claims.
DEL-17-01 source basis is the governing project source-basis authority for downstream PCF claims.
DEL-17-02 export contract is the governing project contract for profile, manifest, ID map, and loss reporting.
The PCF format specification status is TBD; no redistributed proprietary specification text is admitted in this phase.
Engineering design codes and standards are out of scope for this exporter; no code-compliance or professional-approval claim is permitted.
Source-authority verification reviews that each PCF behavior statement cites DEL-17-01, DEL-17-02, PLAN-EXPORT-INTEROP, CAEPIPE-PCF, or project governance sources.
Conservative-profile verification checks that every selected entity family is classified and that unresolved behavior remains TBD.

Writer-behavior verification: future implementation tests shall use invented fixtures and verify supported records are emitted deterministically while unsupported content produces diagnostics/loss entries.

Units/coordinates verification: future tests shall include explicit unit-bearing source data and ambiguous/missing-unit negative cases, profile-bound to declared PCF unit representation, coordinate policy, rejection/diagnostic for missing/ambiguous unit metadata, and no dimensionless fallback for unit-bearing physical values.
Stable-ID verification: future tests shall verify sidecar identity mapping when direct PCF identity carriage is not source-confirmed.
Loss-report verification: future tests shall assert entries for omitted, approximated, delegated, unsupported, and TBD behavior.
Boundary-controls verification reviews for absence of proprietary examples, protected standards data, release claims, compatibility claims, code-compliance claims, and professional-acceptance claims.
The future implementation tranche shall convert the diagnostic/loss-report scaffold into concrete tests only after the PCF profile is sealed, with expected outcome values remaining TBD until then.
Acceptance hook (missing/ambiguous units): diagnostic or blocking loss entry with no silent default for unit-bearing physical values.
Acceptance hook (coordinates/vertical axis): profile-declared coordinate/vertical-axis policy with diagnostic when source coordinate basis is absent or ambiguous.
Acceptance hook (nominal size, OD, wall thickness): export only explicit/source-confirmed attributes where selected; external mapping-database behavior is delegated or loss-reported.
Acceptance hook (material/spec labels): labels emitted only with source-owned provenance; target material-property mapping delegated unless source-confirmed.
Acceptance hook (canonical/target identity): stable ID sidecar or target metadata links canonical IDs to emitted records, omissions, diagnostics, and loss rows; target-generated IDs remain separate.
Acceptance hook (end connections/boundary conditions): free ends, equipment nozzles, adjacent pipelines, and unresolved boundary semantics are blocked, delegated, TBD, unsupported, or loss-reported.
Acceptance hook (supports/restraints): support/restraint transfer is classified separately and loss-reported when not reliably preserved by the selected profile.
Acceptance hook (component approximations): target-side rigid elements, equivalent pipes, concentrated masses, and other simulations are recorded as approximated or delegated behavior.
Acceptance hook (TBD target behavior): TBD remains visible in profile, diagnostics, manifest, or loss report and is blocking when solver-ready or compatibility-sensitive.

The deliverable shall document the PCF subset profile and unresolved target-version basis, supported entity/attribute classes, unsupported/approximated/delegated/omitted/TBD behavior classes, stable ID and sidecar mapping policy, unit and coordinate assumptions, invented fixture provenance, loss-report examples using invented data only, and an explicit limitation that PCF is conservative interoperability only.
